ratings.comment: Wonderful professor, very well respected and one of the only women professors at our school! Cares a lot about issues and topics that do not get explored in architecture, including gender issues. Very helpful with writing tips and thorough in her comments. Definitely take her courses!

Ms. Adams does not have the intellectual means of her ambitions. She has the knack to reduce fascinating subjects to her own despicable understanding. She if you are inquisitive, sensitive and passionate, and I measure my every word, stay away.
decent

Prof. Adams is one of the best teachers I've had. The clarity of her lectures is unsurpassed and she transmits her passion on the subjects that truly interest her. I still think about her lecture on post-modernism and Disney World architecture.  Very approachable, helped me write many scholarship, admission essays by reading them many times over

Simply wonderful - brilliant, clear and eloquent. I was always fascinated by the insightful things she had to say. Enigmatic character. Workload for this class is manageable; make sure to do the readings consistently (otherwise the amount will be difficult to handle for the final). It was a real pleasure taking her class.

Sitting through an Adams lecture is like reading a dictionary. It's informative, but it's dry and sounds like a podcast, with no interaction whatsoever. Her lecture's are well organized and clear, but emotionless and passionless.
Best course I have taken so far at McGill.  Superb lectures, full of personal insights
The best supervisor possible.
An outstanding research methods seminar -- only wish I had taken it years ago.  And Brava on becoming Director of the school.
One of the coolest prof at McGill and very funny too. Notes were very clear and well  explained. Would definitely have her again anytime.
Walked in the first day and said that you'd have to try to fail. She was right :)

This course was extremely well organized. The notes were perfect! The workload was also pretty light. You will definitely find it easy if you can easily picture a 2D image into 3D. Otherwise, practice! Highly recommended

Awesome professor, she gives a personal feel for a class quite large. She is always there to help, makes funny jokes, gives practice exams and is very fair. If you do the practice exams you can ace the midterms :)
You will not regret taking this course!

Great class! Very interesting material. The Prof is great and thus expects you to be, but she provides plenty of tools and material to do well in the course, besides being a great lecturer. Do attend class as she uses a lot of models and these cannot be seen in the recordings.
Great prof. Very clear, very easy to listen to in lectures. Does her best to keep lectures interactive. Exams are extremely fair, so if you keep up there's no reason you shouldn't get an A.
Very good teacher, explains well  and her notes are very helpful.

Nicest prof. at McGill.  Hardworking prof, with plenty of current examples.  Course followed the books and was well laid out.  Exams were fair.  Not enough practice questions or office hours, Moores is always busy, but so friendly.  Overall, great prof.  Take her classes

Not a first, second, nor last choice. If you have to take this course then take it whenever this Prof isn't teaching it. Although midterms and final are pretty easy exams, but you will have a really hard time "SELF" studying for it. I lost my interest in Organic Chemistry after this course. TAs aren't fair in the labs. Lab quizzes are pretty hard.

Just take org 2 as minor and done pretty well with Pavelka's part. Everything were so smooth and well until his appearance. Lecture notes are all over the place, really strong accent. Test the materials on the final that he didn't mention in the lectures at all. All in all, don't take his any course because he doesn't care his students at all
I loved this class.

I loved org.chemI, but he totally destroyed that! Lectures not worth going to, only goes through mechanisms which are in the course pack. Tests horribly detailed, tricky and confusing. The multiple choices are so similar it's hard to tell which one is the right answer. If you have a choice, don't!

His class was so boring. I used to love org chem. He made so ridiculously boring and asked for stupid little details that I lost interest. His lectures are brutal to sit through. Don't go to class. Study the course pack, and go over his slides for any additional info.

Horrible Prof.  His tests are unfair.  He doesn't understand that what you teach in class is what you ought to test on!  His MC is BRUTAL. His accent makes it hard to understand. His slides finished my ink in 2 lectures. Too bad you can't avoid his class....
Lectures were brutal to sit through. Tests were not that difficult, just odd in a way. Overall, destroyed any interest I had in the subject. No Organic 3 for me...

His tests are ridiculous because he spends 90% of his class time going over mechanisms and his exams test you on the little details he brushes over.  He's incredibly tiresome to listen to and makes a difficult subject harder.  Needs to learn IUPAC.  His slides are ridiculous (178/class), image heavy
If you want most useful information in a short time, choose it.

Curtis is the best lecturer I have ever had. If you keep up with the reading and pay attention in class, you will be rewarded with incredible insight from a very passionate, knowledgeable, hilarious professor. If there is an opportunity to take his class, do not miss it.
HE HAS PROMISED GRADES FOUR TIMES. IT IS JANUARY 13. WHERE IS MY FINAL MARK, CURTIS? PLEASE WHERE IS IT

Incredible. So passionate and engaging. He's definitely disorganized and 10 novels is a big load but it's SO WORTH IT. He's hilarious, brilliant, and cares so much. His office hours and feedback are incredibly helpful and he really tries to connect with his students. His lectures take some getting used to but I promise you will learn to love him.

Passionate and articulate guy but very unorganized. Tons of reading for class but little opp to get a word in around him. Lectures can devolve into confusion for students if you zone out for even a second, and nothing is reported or posted electronically. He's amazing one on one but can be frustrating as a lecturer.

He is an awesome prof! Extremely clever, fun and engaging lectures. The reading is rigorous, but enjoyable. The assignments are fair. He is most helpful in office hours. Best ENGL prof I've had during my 4 years.

Really thought provoking lectures, clearly a brilliant guy. You can do well in this class if you dedicate yourself and keep up with the readings (of which there are lots!) I would highly recommend his classes.

Great prof. Approachable, cares about his students. Pace was about a novel a week. Lectures are interesting and he wants to hear what you have to say. Takes a while to return papers because he really combs through and gives thorough feedback. Really honest and open guy, the class had a great vibe

So Professor  Brown is an amazing lecturer, extremely knowledgeable about American Literature. BUT he assigns a ridiculous amount of readings, is extremely disorganized with giving assignments and grading them (although this makes him flexible with deadlines). I would recommend him to anyone who doesn't care about an extremely disorganized semester

Waited months to receive anything back from him. Wrote a midterm in March, still have not received a grade (It's almost September). Wrote my final without any semblance of how I was doing in the class. He is very disorganized, to the detriment of his students. Could not get ahold of him to save my life, but was active on Twitter throughout.

Curtis Brown is one of the best English Literature professors at McGill. His lectures are really engaging, and he is clearly very intelligent. He also makes his classes discussion-based, making the classroom interactive and allowing new, unconventional ideas to be heard. He gives great feedback. He's also hilarious.

She is retiring anyway and I support that she should retire because now nothing innovative would come from her. Her racist attitude would never change since she is a woman in her late 60s or early 70s.

The course was more theoretical. The textbook was rather dull and not elaborative. The assignments were like in high school. We were asked to write a reflection after each class. The Prof is biased at times and she doesn't have strong research expertise. She considered her supervisee from China was better than us but she is just an average student

I would vote the below somewhat negative comments about Prof. Turner. I don't think I fully learned the state-of-the-art mixed method research tools. The course covered more philosophical aspects rather than practical applications. On several occasions, she was explicitly arrogant to me as I'm an international student from a developing country

She is biased and highly racist. The course was so much fixated on mixed methods but lacked practical applications. She claims that she has expertise on quantitative research but in reality she doesn't know statistics. The course was only for doctoral students but it would qualify for MA. If you're non-white and a minority student,don't take her

Carolyn is an kind, helpful and extremely hard-working professor. She gives really detailed and helpful feedback that force you to think and learn a lot. She cares about students and is always responsive. And she would give us really helpful feedback on our presentations. If you devote a proper amount of time in her class, your grade will look fine

Excellent prof. May speak in generalities at times during class, but gives great feedback when approached. Expectations were pretty clear. Softy when it comes to grading. Workload is no practical if you're on internship.
Good prof--funny, enthusiastic, approachable.
Prof. Green is an awesome guy, with a clear passion for herpetology. Fun field trip, interesting lectures, and many different modes of testing - the lab exam is the hardest!

do NOT take biol465. he clearly does not care about the course, has no interest in giving feedback and is unclear in what he expects from you. i took this course of out genuine interest for the topic and i regret it majorly. course as a whole is unorganized, TAs unhelpful, and Green unwilling to do anything about it.
He gives vague or no feedback and admitting his grading of presentations was subjective and pretty random. His lectures were boring and mumbly. Would not recommend taking conservation biology.

No complaints for Green, he definitely is very knowledgeable. However, the course and grading of the course (along with one of the awful TAs) made me regret taking Conservation Biology. I've heard the equivalent at mac is a lot better.

I absolutely adore Donna Lee Smith. She is a truly caring and respectful teacher who takes interests in her students.The class, Communications in educations, is SUPER easy. Not much work is done, and she's a fairly easy marker.Her class is a piece of cake...however most of the work is in groups. I would most defiantly recommend this teacher!

Multicultural education with her was an eye opener and really inspired us.  She's a wise woman, who knows what she's talking about and is able to share stories and experiences relating to the topics at hand.  She can keep you hanging on the entire class! I compare her and her classes to Oprah and her life classes

I love this teacher! This was the second time I had her and she is one of the best in the education program. She loves her subject and knows it very well. She's enabled me to improve my writing and to pay attention to little details that make all the difference!
Take everything with her! A little disorganized, but completely helpful, very interesting, and awesome.
I had Donna Lee for children's lit and she is an amazing teacher! she really enjoys seeing students do well and is always there to help!
Professor Smith is an awesome teacher and I hope to be as lucky as to have her for another class in the future

While I didn't find this professor to be the best lecturer, his slides are super detailed and he gives tons of practice problems which are great preparation for exams. The exams were pretty easy if you practiced and there were no surprises... although the final was waaaay too long. Also, super quick email replies!!!

Good prof! He's clear about what will be on the midterm if you have it. Make sure to pass by his office, and chat with him. He gives good instructions on what you should focus on in terms of question difficulty. Slides are very straight-forward.

Prof Lee makes the lecture enjoyable by all his polls in class. I appreciate his lecture style because I found all those questions we did in class were engaging and helped us understand the material better than simply being lectured. The cons are that we didn't do a midterm, only quizzes, so it was hard knowing what to study for the final.
I did not liked this professor. Although he seems caring and his midterm/assignment is pretty easy, but the final was unexpectedly hard. Also he tries to make the class fun and it doesn't work.

Great professor. My best advice is attend lectures, key to success. You'll build on knowledge class after class. Not the most entertaining prof, though he jokes sometimes. But, very concrete, illustrates with examples and past final questions. Easy midterm, but hard assignment (both 20%). Final was more difficult and challenging than expected (60%)

Lee was so so so great, choose him choose him choose him! Although only winter term he has mgcr 211, never miss to register his class! The assignment helps you to have a better idea of how to evaluate a financial statement. Also, the mid-term is really a cake.  Final is hard, but if you prepared all exercise, you are fine, because he will curve up!
He really cared about the students. Tried to make an introductory accounting class as interesting and engaging as possible. If you have to take MGCR 211, I strongly recommend Dongyoung.

Professor Lee was a great prof and I would 100% recommend taking MGCR 211 with him above others (I've heard plenty of nightmares from students about other accounting profs). As long as you do the past exams which he provides before the exam you'll be fine. TBH this midterm was a cake walk and the final was brutal but that's what the curve is for.

Professor Lee is great! He definitely knows how to keep the class interesting despite the pretty dry topic and makes lots of great jokes! Final hasn't happened yet but the midterm was pretty easy as long as you practice, and he provided lots of past exams which were very similar to the actual exam. Great course!
Super kind and funny prof who manages to make accounting interesting and enjoyable. Highly recommend!

Professor Lee is a very caring professor and his jokes help make the content so much more enjoyable to learn. It's also clear he cares about his students and he wants us to succeed. He also provides lots of practice materials from past exams which are nearly identical to the exam itself, which is suuuper nice and makes it much easier to succeed

A caring man, I like Professor Dongyoung Lee. He was responsive to emails, and it is obvious he cares about his students. However, I do think he struggled with online classes this semester, making ridiculously hard midterm exams that took many hours to complete. While his grading evaluation was whack this semester, I do like him as a person.

Definitely one of the better accounting profs in the faculty. Drops a ton of hints for midterms and finals, exams are always fair as long as you practice the past midterms he provides, and his lectures are always interesting and his passion definitely comes through in them. He really cares about his students and it shows.

Possibly one of the most caring professors at McGill. His lectures are a joy, he churns through the material and always makes sure that the entire class is engaged. If I was to go into accounting, I would want to be taught by him and him only. He really wants students to do well and is extremely chill. Exams are fair and he always drops hints.

He is a great lecturer who keeps students engaged with questions but also tells about 5 corny dad jokes per class and they're hilarious. Will answer emails promptly. He is adorable and funny and a genuine good guy who wants students to succeed. As a life science taking this course in my final year, he is by far my favorite professor at McGill!
Chill dude. Wants to help students. Wants students to learn, enjoy and score well. Hilarious!!! Would definitely take him again 100%!!!

Professor Lee is a super cool prof. He really takes care of his students and, even if his subject is hard for most of us, he makes it easier to succeed. Work a lot and you will have a good grade. He makes jokes and answers fast to emails. Would recommend 10/10 if you have to take this class.

Prof. Lee wants you to do well, that's for sure. Class felt very lecture heavy, but he checks to make sure everyone understood. Exams were exactly what was shown in class, but sometimes material felt rushed. Practice exams normally provided.

Great teacher, super helpful. Very kind and you can tell he loves what he does! He has a lot of knowledge in the field and will answer all your questions until you finally understand. He's also adorable!

Might not have a "clear" English but very good and amazing prof! Always there for you. Answers email in 10 minutes at 2am! Gives a lot of hints for exams and assignments to make your life way more easy. Not only a good prof but extremely funny and adorable. You can expect to participate a lot since he uses clickers to engage students! Take him!
He speaks a lot about exam contents, it is very helpful
I think he is a very good professor. He is trying to make accounting interesting with real-life examples in class.
I like him a lot. He is very helpful and tries to simplify the material as much as possible. However the midterm was brutal. It was too long.
Prof Lee is incredibly nice and dedicated to his students. Always willing to help out his students. His lecture is very clear and helpful.
SO boring
Really great teacher who truly cares about her students. Lectures are easy to understand and conferences are easy to get credit for.
Needs to assign readings that are suitable for the class.

While she has a large background in African History and is evidently passionate about it, she has a lot of work to do in becoming a good prof. She reads almost word for word off of her slides and does not connect ideas, slides, or anything else very well. The readings were very large and well ahead of a 200 level course

A great prof who is passionate about the material. I learned a lot even though I only took it as an elective -- might go into history after all. Clear lectures and fair grading. She was really helpful outside of class too. Hard work but if you read and pay attention you'll do well.

Did not like the format of this class - lectures were hard to pay attention to because she read off the slides most of the time. For evaluation 15% based on BBC pod-casts(ONE current news source for a history course??), heavy readings for conference papers which took way too much time for the amount they were worth (about 3%)/for a 200-level.

Although she has a lot of passion for African History, she is very disorganized in lectures and only reads her notes word for word. This leads to her jumping all over the place and can be hard to follow. Only her first year tohugh

Amazing professor. Perhaps the best I've ever had. He is fair, caring and captivating. Other teachers should learn from him. He does make you work for your grade. The assignments are pretty long, but very useful and clear. The same goes for the exams. You can tell he really wants you to learn and become the best version of yourself.

10 hours after the final was due, he finished grading it all. 'Nuff said. There are 11 assignments and they are quite hard. However, he allows you to check answers with your friends, and he won't hesitate to give you hints if you ask for it. He's there for a solid 30 minutes before and after class for office hours. Good analogies behind concepts.
In terms of professorship, Adrian Liu defines perfection.
Adrian is such an awesome and amazing prof!! He is caring and always encourages his students. In terms of pedagogy, he is one of the best teachers I've ever met. 100% recommend his course!!

Best prof I've ever had! He has the ability to explain hard materials well in lectures, and he responses to all your questions in great detail (you may see a two-page response for a very short question) and immediately (I once got an email response on 4:30am). You can also see what your peers asked on the "question slip response" which helps a lot!

His weekly problem sets were time-consuming, but very reasonable and doable because he did an awesome job teaching the material. If some question was too hard, he would give useful hints when asked for help rather than letter the student struggle with a wrong method.
When decades will pass and I would forget almost everything from McGill, I will still remember Adrian as THE BEST.
The best

Prof. Liu is simply the perfect teacher. Not only does he truly care about his students and his pedagogy, but he also knows his stuff inside and out. Do the assignments, follow his criteria, and you'll get an A, as you should. I would hope that all physics students that take this class take it with him.
best teacher you could hope to have.

He's my Physics hero!!! 100% best professor at McGill! Very detailed statements and explanations in class, sometimes hilarious, and designs excellent assignments for you to prepare for the exams. He's also a fast grader, you will get the feedback of the assignments every week on time, and it only took 1 day for him to grade final.

What else can be said ? very helpful and amazing professor with awesome lectures. Lectures are very informative and entertaining. He gives an excellent foundation for relativity and quantum mechanics. I am surely going to miss those phys260 lectures

Quite literally the greatest professor I have had at McGill, probably the best I will have. He cares about his students' well being, understanding and success, he is accessible outside of class and readily available to answer questions, and he gives homework that is as doable and instructive as it is challenging. I would give him a 100/5 if I could

His ability to explain seemingly difficult subjects and make them seem graspable is amazing. Lectures are very informative and fun. You know he cares about the students' learning when he lets students hand in question slips and answers them. If ratemyprof allowed a 100/5 rating, then that would be the case.

Amazing amazing prof. I can't even begin to explain how awesome he is; you'll just have to take him. I highly recommend taking his class; he cares about students, the lectures are amazing and engaging, and he's the sweetest person ever. The class is hard, but you'll leave having learnt so much and having a blast in class!

Best Professor EVER, 5.0 is not enough for him! I would give him 100/5.0. Personally, I'm not a physics student and take this as one of my complementary classes. The lectures are great and he explains every super well. The material is tough by itself but he and the TAs are always available to help you out.

Adrian is the best professor I had in McGill. His lectures are fun and crystal clear. He promotes learning and encourages students to ask questions and work hard in order to master the material. He cares about the students and responds to emails quickly. Class is by no means easy as there are challenging weekly problem sets but the effort pays off.

He restores hope in me that academia is not filled with heartless old profs who see students as an obstacle to a high h-index. He hands out optional anonymous feedback slips at the beginning of each class and answers any questions you've written on them after class. He tries to perfect himself as a lecturer, but I think he's there.
Great professor, breaks down the concepts to make them very understandable. The lectures were interesting, so was the group project.

Hes the man! Highly recommend for Business Statistics. Clear lectures and a caring guy  makes good jokes, too! He provides great in-class examples and extra practice questions to help prepare for exams. I may take Advanced Business Statistics just to be taught by him again.

Solid Professor. Slides were great. Interesting talking to. Only thing I would have liked is more support, especially during the midterm and final exams, but other then being somewhat absent, a good statistics professor.
Terrible! He's mean and unclear
Javad is an incredible professor. His slides are very clear. To do well in this course, follow the lectures and do the practice questions that the professor is going to give you.
He's awesome.

Not a lot of people like Business Stats because it's pretty difficult. Although, Javad explains the material super well, he always does examples in class and he gives out assignments that help you prepare for exams which is great. I think he was a new teacher at McGill when I got him but he did a super good job.
Too hard for me as a student with pure business background

I don't have a business background so these concepts were new and challenging. Quizzes and Exams were difficult. People in our class scored half of the answers correctly. One of the TAs was a tough grader. Some people ask questions multiple times in the class and he will say mean things to humiliate you, which I did not like. But I did learn a lot.

His lectures were a lot of reading off slides which were just not my cup of tea, and his worked examples weren't always the clearest. The 2 midterms were pretty fair but the final definitely required some very good understanding of the course material and combining things in ways you hadn't seen in class.

Professor Li is very caring and you can tell he really wants the students to understand. Even for a course he claimed to be relatively "boring" for him, he still puts in a lot of effort to teach every lesson clearly and go over many examples in class. He does good review before exams and is takes feedback seriously. Great professor!

He was one of the sweetest professors I've ever had. He genuinely cares about helping you understand the course material, and doesn't make it unnecessarily hard for no reason. Not an easy A, but you can get there if you do the practice problems and show up to class.

Jianyu really does his best! He takes complaints very seriously and is constantly improving his teaching methods, and his exams difficulty level. Besides that, he's passionate, cares about his student, and is actually good at explaining the material if you really pay attention to what he's doing in class.

I actually like Jianyu even though I didn't do great in his class. I feel like that was more on me, he provides all the materials to do well, you just need to take initiative and study in your own time. His midterms were a bit tough, but not so bad that you wouldn't be able to still do well in the course. He's a good guy

Very good prof, clear explanations and excellent power-points. Midterms are a bit hard because of the lack of time. Need to do a lot of practice for the midterms and have the concepts clearly in your head so that you don't hesitate. Final is not necessarily easier in terms of difficulty but time is not an issue. Textbook is also useful.

His lectures are solid, but you'll probably have to review the material outside of class to do well. He is a caring, reasonable professor, and he obviously wants the students to do well. He's really helpful in office hours, and will be more than willing to give you the time of day if you seek him out.

Horrible teacher, I would wait for the next semester to take the class with another teacher if I were you. Made the class hard for no reason and does not explain clearly. Only did well cause I taught the class to myself with the textbook.

The grading scheme of the course was stressful since it was basically just 2 midterms and a final. I found his midterms much more challenging than the final exam which was written by the prof in the mechanical engineering section. However, Jianyu Li is very caring and wants students to do well. Hated it at the time but would take again!
I find Jianyu is a good prof. Clear and easy to work with, but the midterms are a big tough.

Jianyu somehow made simple mechanics complicated. His tests did not correlate with his class examples. NEED to read the textbooks, or else you won't get a good grade. Also he does not understand/ answer questions, he brushes them off as remarks. He basically forces you to go to office hours.
AVOID AT ALL COSTS

He was quite rude and arrogant. He was a VERY bad professor (but thank god for youtube and the textbook). His midterms were unreasonable, not enough time to blink/breathe in between questions. AVOID AT ALL COSTS, unless you wear your Harvard sweatshirt to class.
His tests were too long and unclear and not comparable to the in class material, most of the material in class you will need to review by yourself from the textbook. Avoid if you can.

he's kind of awkward in the best way possible, and some of the things he says just end up being hilarious. very straight-forward and to-the-point, his exams are exactly as how he says they will be. he goes through every example very thoroughly, clear slides/writing, and tries to make mechanical engineering relevant to bioengineering

Not helpful outside of class, didn't show up his office hour right before midterm. Crazy long final exam, you wouldn't pass if you did bad on midterms. Course organization was overall pretty bad, TAs not helpful at all. Avoid!
The professor did his best to convey and manage the course materials. Midterms and final I took were very reasonable. Recommended
Prof. Li was very sweet and helpful even outside of lecture hours. The course material isn't super easy but he was pretty patient at walking me through problems from start to finish.
He is a great and caring professor.

Clear grading criteria. This course had higher weightage for project. Need not attend all the classes, but strongly recommend you to attend the lectures as it is useful for the final examination. This professor takes a lot of efforts to make the class interesting and is really passionate about the subject.

This professor is amazing, I would definitely take him again. Levy has a great culture that he will share with you in a very engaging manner. His sarcastic humor is not for everyone, nor is his very heavy reading workload. But overall I am so glad that I took this course, even if I am not a polisci major. I learned so much.

Levy's lectures are engaging, and he adapted to the online format of the class by making small, 15 minutes segments to watch and keep students interested. He makes political theory concepts very accessible. This class is one of the best POLI classes at McGill thanks to him. Getting a good grade isn't impossible if you put in the work for it.

Levy is a great lecturer and a fairly reasonable grader, which makes the content more digestible. Still, I regret taking two classes with him because of the way he toes the line between educator and aspiring-thought-leader. I don't believe he cares about his students nearly as much as he enjoys having a captive audience.

The prof was interesting and so was the material to a certain extent but I feel like this was a terrible "Introduction" to political theory. Also, it was terribly organized! The papers were graded very harshly and there very little feedback given. Discussion boards were very difficult to navigate. Would not recommend!!

Fascinating course, fascinating prof. The best aspect of it are the lectures, short and frequent. Instead of having to plough through 2 hour lectures, I could sit down and choose which 15 minute snippet I would watch at a time, and having one topic for every lecture was beautiful to go back to. Prof clearly knows his stuff also.

No synchronous lectures this year, so POLI 231 felt like an afterthought after attending other, more engaging courses. More particular about grammar conventions and structure than instructors at the 300/400 level. Content was interesting, but it's an absurd amount of reading every week. Don't take as an elective, and expect to put in a lot of work!

Levy's lectures were boring and disengaging. The format of the course wasn't too bad but the readings were brutally boring and the weekly conferences were a pain. Wouldn't take again but he wasn't terrible.

Professor Levy was very considerate about the pandemic and our mental health which was amazing. The course was very interesting but a bit heavy for a first year. The readings can be overwhelming but you'll finish this course with soo much knowledge!

Prof Levy is clearly a passionate person who knows what he is talking about, he is also quite approachable. The class has many weekly readings that re often more than 25 pages long. The syllabus is clear and helpful too. However, the grading is surprisingly harsh and little to no feedback is given (this might have to do with the TAs, I don't know).

(Online Class) Definitely reading heavy, multiple readings per week and the lectures can be a bit long. However I enjoyed the material, Prof Levy was clearly knowledgeable and even though the lectures were sometimes tough to get through, they were always interesting content and presentation wise. Also papers heavy, grade wise.

The material was kind of engaging but since it was a recorded lecture it felt a little distant. Office hours were okay. Content was kind of boring but I think that's got to do with political philosophy in general. Discussion boards weren't organised that well and the TA wasn't very helpful. The papers were graded very harshly which was depressing.
Amazing lecturer but tons of readings...

Prof. Levy is an amazing lecturer! There are a bunch of readings and I seriously suggest you doing as many as you can because you will need to do them for the 3 essays anyway and it is hard to catch up at the last minute. Also if you have done the readings when going to class his lectures will be so much more helpful, he really explains a lot.

He gives excellent lectures, which I've found to be very informative. I didn't find him pompous at all, just very direct. Definitely not a great starting point for U0 students, should really be a 300-400 class. You'll read yourself to death. But interesting subject matter, and his subtle, kind of dark, but very funny humour underlines it all.

Professor Levy s a really clear and captivating orator. He does not use slides and makes you read a lot but it is all well-thought out and cohesive with what he talks about in class. I highly recommend taking poli 231 if you are interested in the philosophy behind politics and how we choose to organize ourselves in society. This class changes you.
He is a good prof but was definitely a prof more for the upper levels and was a bit of an adjustment as a U0 student.

Amazing lecturer with a humorous side you won't get to see as often as you would like. Super knowledgeable about what he is teaching. Tough grading however, did not meet many people who got above B+ in their essays.

Would recommend ONLY if you are in your second year or higher and have decided to major in poli sci! He is a great lecturer, but not super accessible outside class. Reading materials are interesting but too much and too deep for a 200 level course. My TA was really nice and smart, yet it is very hard to get enough help on either reading or writing.

Intelligent (if pretentious) guy, great orator, but lectures are hard to follow and grading seems extremely tough unless you essentially present the same argument as in the readings? Would not recommend unless you're in poli sci and/or want to pursue political theory.

While his lectures were very interesting and actually quite good, he is ridiculously pompous and pretentious. He clearly thinks he's super intelligent and that this material is the most interesting thing in the world. He also marks way too hard for a 200 class and considerably harder than any of the other professors that teach this course.

It's a shame because for the most part I do enjoy his lectures, however he has a super off-putting personality. He treats the students like babies, making TAs go around to tell people to get off their phones and scolding people who are talking. I felt like I was in grade 9 in his class. For the lectures, I wish he would ground them a bit more

Amazing, amazing, AMAZING! Easily my favorite prof. His lectures actually make you want to wake up at 8:30 in the morning and come to class. You have to work for your grade, but the material is extremely interesting. If you're a poli sci student, this class under this prof is a MUST.

Prof. Levy is an incredible lecturer and Intro to Political Theory was the most inspiring course I have taken so far at McGill. I couldn't help but hang onto his every word in lectures and he was there for me when I needed further explanation. That being said, the course is very demanding so only take it if the subject interests you.

His lectures are well thought out though they didn't "blow my mind" like some other students seemed to believe. He loads on too many readings without proper attention given to each in order to make it worth my time. Grades too hard for a 200 level. Thankfully i got a good TA. He brought doughnuts once though... that was cool.

Very good lectures, despite the early class. Helped students whenever possible, but mostly was the duty of the TAs to help clarify things. A fair amount of reading through the term. Truly great orator, as the comments below will tell you. Essays required depth and good understanding of the texts, but not impossibly difficult to get a decent grade.

Amazing orator, sheer brilliance yet no pedantry, 8.30 lectures yet the most enjoyable of the week by far, wish they'd last hours. Interesting conferences, challenging papers, grading is quite severe. Lots of readings, have to do them to keep but they're all very interesting. Gotta attend class to.

Great speaker, horribly pompous. He frequently just summarizes texts, but the other half of the time he's blowing your mind. Paper topics are really hard, and my TA was a crazy tough grader, no good feedback. Kind of turned me off political theory - it was interesting, but just not that interesting. Have to go to class.

Loved him! Sparked my love for political theory. Won't miss a single lecture even though it's an 8:30 am. Brilliant guy, so much respect. It isn't easy to get a good grade though. Make sure your writing is up to par.
Never, never never AGAIN! He does not care about his students.

I still think about years later I taken his class and he remains one of my least favourable moment of all my undergrad experience. I remember going to his office hours for feedbacks as to the research paper, and he answers "everything is on the assignment instructions". Professor Jacob, you don't the essence of teaching as in guiding YOUR students.

This prof is easily my favourite of all time. He is incredibly smart, well-spoken, and a captivating lecturer. Cares deeply about his students too. If you take his class though get ready to read; readings can sometimes exceed 100 pages lol. Loved
By far the best lecturer I've ever seen. Every class is mind-blowing.
Get ready to read, really. He's a good prof and should be respected by us, he also helps us out a lot when you visit him during his office hours. Horrible and difficult as f papers though.

Jacob Levy is easily one of the best orators you will ever take at McGill. He makes the material difficult and he will challenge you to be sure but he is a reasonable grader. A little pretentious but deservedly so. Take every class you can get with him.

Excellent professor. Really cared about the class, and you could tell he was excited about the material. He cultivated a wonderful academic atmosphere where students felt encouraged to express their opinions, but not without rigorously defending their point. Professors like him are truly the reason I'm in academia.

Prof Levy is an incredibly knowledgeable, patient, and involved professor. Speaking from a graduate level, he encourages freedom in class discussion while also trying to mediate and keep dialogue on point.  He is an incredibly encouraging and helpful professor. I would definitely recommend his classes, I've no doubt they will be enriching for you!

to pass this class GO TO TUTORIALS. her exam questions are quite literally from the tutorials and the crowdmark assignments. sometimes you'll be able to find solutions to the exam questions in the textbook since the exams are open book. the class is hard but if you do well on the long answer questions you should be fine.
This course is very difficult, and she doesn't make it seem easier. She presents the material as it is, but tries to make it more engaging. Midterms and final were both very difficult.

Professor Liu is very nice but her lectures are not as direct as they should be. She gives a lot of useful ressources. GO TO TUTORIALS, use the practice problems, do your homework and have your formulas with you before exams. Shes very fair so you should have a good grade with some efforts. Class seems tough at 1st but youll get used to it.
Prof. Liu is really an amazing professor! She really makes the online courses adorable.

She really tries to make the class entertaining but at the end of the day, the material is just not fascinating. The notes are practically just theory (no exam-like questions covered in class). The tutorials are most important to pass the class. The tutorial problems & assignment problems are types of questions that resemble the midterm and final.

The professor is a nice person and she is accessible; will always answer questions. She tries her best to make the class fun and engaging, but her lectures are just very stale. Tutorials is what matters most for this class, thats where youll learn the content. Also her final exam was insanely difficult when compared to tests and assignments.

Her explanation is not good enough , so you should study by your self and based on her notes. The assignments are difficult to do just with the course material ,so you should investigate by yourself. At the end , the course I not great but you can learn about useful things.

i regret taking this class, stay away from her classes by all means. shes not organized, not enough practice questions and she treats everyone differently. her class is a waste of time and you cannot rely on her notes. I can only imagine how her exam will look like and this is coming from an A student
A professor who is good at using her power. She requested me of writing letters to the department for the nomiation of the Award for Distinguished Teaching.
Professor Laura is so nice and kind! She is also a really great teacher and I learned a lot of French during this course. It's not too difficult if you stay on top of all of the assignments.

Her lectures were very unorganized and repetitive. Her feedback is very unclear, making learning very frustrating. The homework assignments were long. Tests were also very long and difficult, regardless of how little or how much you studied. Avoid!

She was a great prof. There's quite a bit of work, but the number of assignments mean that messing up a few times doesn't tank your grade. She responded quickly to any emails and always gave detailed feedback. The key to doing well in this course is studying from home - it was a flipped classroom, so most of the actual class was practice.

Laura is really kind and cares that you learn. The class was 3 hours long, but she didn't lecture very much so we were participating a lot and staying engaged. Super good teacher with very organized course material and clear expectations. Not too much work at all - very manageable, especially if you stay on it.

Very boring course
Bad
Madame Bourrel is very nice! Personally, did not find her class that useful for improving my french, but still a helpful teacher that I would love to have again.

Laura Bourrel was one of the kindest profs I've ever had! Her class is designed for success and is not unnecessarily stressful. If you participate and follow the rubrics she provides for assignments then you'll do well! This class was at 8:30am, but honestly, I didn't even mind because it was entertaining and I felt like going was worthwhile!

I really liked Prof Hunters class, he was personable and funny, and though 226 didn't focus on the architecture aspect as much as I wish it had, I think that that's more of a result of a vague class structure than a failure on his part. I liked him a lot and would recommend one of his classes even for a first time ARTH student
Best ARTH prof at McGIll

People on here are right about his lecture style being unusual and hard to follow, but hes a real sweetie! Very passionate about your passions and gives great feedback! Super funny and kind, has very interesting ideas even though they can be hard to understand at first. Reread notes before tests and itll all come together

I love prof Hunter! He was funny and sweet, but I agree with other reviews; you definitely want to take another intro course before taking this one. The material was interesting but taking notes was really painstaking. You will get readings but he often references it in the lectures so if you take good notes you won't HAVE to read them.

Very caring and understanding prof, but his intro class is too hard. Weekly lectures and readings are long and heavy; it is very easy to fall behind. He is a lenient grader however and you will learn a lot from his class.

Prof. Hunter is very knowledgeable and passionate about 18th century art. However, the lectures were extremely difficult to follow. The language he uses is very academic and his lectures can be convoluted. His class made art history seem intimating and inaccessible which is discouraging considering this is an intro level class.

Hunter is a wonderful prof and I'd definitely recommend every art hist major try to take at least one class with him! Super caring and funny! The only thing I wish he did differently was maybe ground some of the lectures with more context, there are a lot of themes and it sometimes gets confusing/overwhelming

Great professor, very passionate and smart. BUT, this "intro" class was supposed to be my elective and it ended up being my hardest class. For the first month or two I had no idea what he was talking about but it starts getting clearer around the end. A few pop quizzes, open notes midterm and final and a research paper. Interesting but hard.

he is one of the most confusing profs I have ever had. This is a 200 level course and he speaks to us like we all have a PhD. I do not understand a single thing he is talking about in class and the readings he assigns are stupid. It sounds like it could be interesting but he does not touch at all on architecture. DO NOT TAKE THIS COURSE!!!

Really great prof! Super interesting if you do the readings and follow along in class. No laptop policy so if that's a deal breaker for you... Some quizzes but they aren't terrible if you keep up. Readings aren't too long and many of them are posted online so it won't break the bank.
Difficult for first-year students. Remember to take down as many things he mentioned in the class as possible. He is willing to answer questions after class.

Wow, this is probably the worst Art History intro class at McGill. It's supposed to be an ''intro'' class, but it feels like a 400 level one. The readings are not always related to the paintings. The teacher has a PhD and speaks to you as though assuming you know everything already. This is not teaching. Also, he often runs out of time. Come on.

Amazing prof, he is very passionate about the subject and therefore the lectures are interesting. As previously mentioned, his course contains many abstract ideas, but just try to follow along and if you have any difficulties he is more than happy to assist you.

He has a grandiose way of speaking, but once you get past that, along with his strange links between topics, his lectures are fascinating. Make sure you pay full attention in class or you WILL be lost. He's quirky and fun, once you get accustomed to his lectures, making for an enjoyable class. Matthew Hunter is the kind of prof that grows on you.

Excellent prof. Unbelievable course. While if you stop paying attention for even a second in class you can lose your place (has a tendency to be convoluted), if you commit yourself to listening to what he has to say and do the readings, you'll be sucked into the lectures. Fulfilling class, learned a lot from him.

Lectures were very hard to keep up with - you don't know what points he's making and how they connect with each other until the end. That said, keep up with the readings and he TELLS you exactly what he wants on the essay and exams!

Very passionate and knowledgeable about what he teaches, but his slides were all over the place and it was very hard to follow. The readings are lengthy and often hard to understand. AVOID if you're taking this as an elective

A great professor! He's clearly enthusiastic and passionate about his subject. The readings (although there can be a pretty large amount of them) are fascinating and so are the pieces of art that we looked at! He encourages participation from students and is interested in your opinion. You need to work hard for this course, but it's worth it!
Best Prof! My favorite class of the semester! So passionate about the subject and was looking forward to his class every day. Also very fair grader.

A great prof! Passionate, funny, smart. I like him as much as Hilsdale. The readings are interesting and relevant, and really not that hard to keep up with. He likes you to challenge yourself, so don't go for the easiest topic and put in some extra research for the paper, it'll show in your grade!
Really difficult to follow. Lots of reading. Beware.

Hunters classes are hard. However, he is very compassionate with his students and rarely gives bad graves; he makes up for the hard readings/content. However I would only recommend him for ARTH students bc his language is very specific and complez. Assignments are straight forward and gives great feedback and ideas to help u grow as a scholar.:)

He is a super caring guy but is just not a good lecturer. I usually left his lectures more confused than simply reading the dense papers assigned for class because his lectures were so all over the place. Class is also supposed to be only 3 hours a week and he posted 4, 30-60 min lectures a week on top of the mandatory 60 minute live class.

Prof. Hunter asks questions that put you outside of your comfort zone, which seems to be intimidating at first but could lead to very fruitful discoveries if you put in the work to think outside of the box and make bold connections. Absolutely inspirational and super caring and understanding
Genius

Matthew is a passionate professor, and genuinely cares about his students. This seminar was experimental, ambiguity was to be expected. However, it was discouraging throughout the semester taking this class as expectations were unclear, and course themes were unstably addressed. In the end, it was a fulfilling course; but more guidance was needed.

Prof. Hunter is genuine and kind: You can tell he truly cares about each of his students. He is passionate about what he does, which, admittedly can result in niche (even esoteric) lectures- but this is not a bad thing. He is excited about each topic covered and eager to connect with and listen to his students. A gem of McGill Art History!

I took a linguistics course with this prof whose specialty is french literature so i'll cut him some slack, but overall I thought his class was extremely boring but also very easy. Grading scheme consisted of 2 in-class exams, 1 take-home exam, and participation. This class reminded me of high school (had us do practice Qs in class in groups).

Prof speaks so quietly that you can barely make out what he's saying no matter where you're sitting in class. His lectures always consisted of one slide and were super repetitive. Boring as hell, didn't learn a thing all semester. Easy enough though, only 2 tests and 1 final project, based on the slides & textbook. I definitely wouldn't recommend.

Great class but could be more challenging. The slides are a bit stodgy sometimes (everything's posted on MyCourses though) Prof. Diouf is attentive to his students and so calm! You need to insist sometimes to get clear answers but he's very approachable (go see him at his office hours) and responds quickly to his emails. Also, not a tough grader!

Wouldn't necessarily recommend the class to english speaking people, as there are group projects and you're also invited to participate quite a lot. Otherwise, cool and not very fast-paced course. Diouf is nice and calm, and he answers very quickly to his emails too! Overall, good intro to francophone literature.

Don't know about his linguistics course but the francophone literature course is definitely not a big deal (four of five novels to read during the semester and easy quizzes). Nice, caring and relaxed prof! Gives great feedback when he's asked (I agree with the previous review: go see him during his office hours!)

Prof cool. Les exams sur les livres ne sont pas vraiment compliqués et le cours n'est pas non plus d'une grande difficulté. Les thèmes abordés sont parfois un peu trop larges, mais M. Diouf se rattrape largement grâce à l'attention portée aux étudiants et à leurs questions. Super accessible, sympa et très humain!

Amazing prof. He will tell you exactly what to expect for his short tests (each worth 30%), a presentation, and a final based on the short tests. He is really passionate and makes you want to read and question more the material, thus developing your own critical thoughts. 100% WOULD TAKE HIM AGAIN.

Melanie is an amazing person and clearly very knowledgeable. However, she's very disorganized which makes the group projects stressful. Her lectures are good, guest speakers were also great. She's extremely understanding of personal situations and flexible with deadlines. Don't buy the textbook, you don't really need it.

Melanie is a nice person, and is very kind and understanding, but not a great teacher for Indigenous Education at least. The lectures were vague and I ultimately didn't learn anything about Indigenous education. All we did was read articles, have TPS activities, and the class turned into an SJW fest. It seemed like she had 0 knowledge of Indig. ed.

Melanie is a great prof. Always listening to students and their concerns. She is very chill but also covers all the material needed. 50% of the grade is based on group projects and graded pretty harshly. Overall this class was great, but half of my classes this semester got cancelled or put online last minute. Not an easy A...

Very disorganized! Due to personal issues, half the semester was online and class was often cancelled minutes before. Instructions were unclear for big assignments + over 5 small reflections (5% each) that required HOURS of work. Thankfully, due to these circumstances, she was understanding with deadlines. Sweet teacher but would not do it again :/

Melanie is awesome and she is the most realistic education prof I've come across. People will label her as disorganized for having flexible deadlines but the reality is that you're going to do well regardless as long as you submit your assignments. Her flexibility saved my mental health during my field experience so I would recommend her to anyone.

I had her for Professional Seminar in third year. Although this was a mandatory class she cancelled more than 75% of classes. I only went 3 times the whole semester. She's a very caring and funny person but she does postpone a lot of assignment and is somewhat disorganized. But she is very easy and chill.
LOVE her! Best nicest teacher! So CARING <3

Quite honestly the kindest and most considering person I have ever met. She is so fantastic and teaches you so much. For ELA she is flexible and gives many great opportunities for you to be the one teaching. In Indigenous education, she brings in many Indigenous guest speakers and offers them a platform to share their experiences.
She is very caring and flexible with deadlines. A very understanding prof, would for sure take a course with her again.

Such a sweet and caring teacher! However, she is a bit disorganized at times. Most of the coursework is group projects. She is understanding and flexible with deadlines. There is also a lot of reading.
Melanie is the best. She is always there to help and gives such good writing exercises to use in the classroom. I love her, the best. the best. the best. :):):):):)

Mel is caring and understanding that you have a life outside of class. That said, it's almost Jan 6th and I haven't received any grades from assignments done from Oct-Dec. I have received one grade from an assignment worth 5%. She says she'll return grades quickly as she teaches us to do with our students but she didn't practice what she preached.

Beware if you're not good at maths, the only reason I passed this class was that he curved up the final grades. The class was very difficult, very heavy in material and the tests were harsh, particularly on the maths, and didn't leave us with enough time to finish. He has an extremely monotone voice, I just couldn't stay awake during class...

If you are not good with memorizing, don't take this class. The only way I got my A was through strict memorization. There are also math equations that you will have to learn and apply on the final exam. Avoid taking him if you're taking other heavy courses at the same time, as it requires lots of your time. He curves the final grades though.

This class covers so much material, which is very poorly explained. Class average was very low and close to everyone was struggling. The final was cumulative and very hard, and was worth 70% of our grade. A lot of reading, loads of concepts and math. Do not recommend unless mandatory.

If you don't have to take his classes, don't... Final exam is worth 60% and covers everything from the beginning. Very harsh grader (highest grade in the class was 80). Smith is however very knowledgeable

Absolutely terrible lecturer. Learned all the course content from textbook. Powerpoint slides are a mess and just blocks of dense text. Smith is not accessible and grades exceptionally hard for a 200-level prereq course. How is the average a B-...... do not reccomend ever. stay clear

Dr. Smith is not great... to put it lightly. Questions for participation grade were mandatory, however, he was very condescending in his answers to any questions asked. Was not an encouraging environment and the material was very boring. Very statistics-heavy by the second half of the semester. No offence but the dude just needs to retire.

Designated a portion of the grade to Q & A, however, no matter the question as he was extremely condescending in his answer. Not a good teacher, does not care about students- needs to retire lets leave it at that. Do not take a class with him unless you have to.
Horrible
He is very arrogant when you ask questions. Does not provide feedback on test. I like his accent but that is all. Very old school in his way of thinking...

i am taking him online and i still don't know what to expect, he is unclear and very dismissive of students questions yet wants you to ask them at all cost... no guidelines for tests and his powerpoint slides are like novels... for an intro class he is really rude and goes too fast.. this course i am still not sure what it is about...

His style is v old school, and this may require some adjustment. Sit back and enjoy him talk. To study, follow the notes he posts online, they're very clear and you don't need anything else to get an A. It helps if you have entry-level background in stats (from cegep or another course at mcgill) to understand certain sections, but not required.

Worst class and prof I ever took. Avoid at all costs if you can. Lectures are really hard to follow (he uses chalk to write notes), cannot understand him when he speaks, so much material and barely any of it is tested on. So much work for a 200 level class. He also is very stand off-ish and does not help at all.

He is a nice and friendly person and the exam questions are do-able and simple however there is way way way too much stuff to study for them. Since there are only two exams and a billion notions and theories, for the first midterms we had to learn by heart and I mean by heart theories and material from aprox 200 slides too much!!!!!!!!!!

Old school but amazing lectures. Only one midterm and a final so no room for error but study well and you'll be fine. didn't use the textbook, but could be useful if not used to this type of lecturing.

Stay away if possible! This professor somehow made an intro class the most confusing class I've taken. The final is worth 60% and is all short answer. He stated that he would provide a formula sheet, however, asked questions requiring formulas that were not provided. This class, when taught by Smith, is very disorganized. Rely on textbook!!

Not great but not terrible. He doesn't use a lot of visuals in class and so it can be kind of hard to follow lecture. Uses good examples but if you're lost on a concept there goes the lecture. Better off reading the textbook. Pretty simple midterm/final if you study but we get very little information on how we're graded.

I usually don't write reviews, but I thought I had to speak out to tell everyone how nice and caring this professor is!!! I really don't get why the others are being so harsh... He is really patient and caring. He is such a nice man! His lectures are long, but he is willing to spend whatever time needed for us to understand the topic. LOVED HIM!!!

A professor who truly doesn't actually care about your academic improvement as a student. I might as well have bought the textbook and read it on my own time. He flat-out refused to answer questions about the final exam in class, and had his TA's "clarify" what would be on the exam the night before it was held. Rude, apathetic, and disorganized.

Students this semester were forced to review the material (approx. 4) chapters on their own as it was barely covered in lecture. While the material itself is not too difficult to grasp, its disappointing for those dependent on good lecture notes or looking for a professor who is accommodating out of class time.

While the professor is clearly knowledgeable in the subject, his intelligence is shrouded by his stronger interest in pursuing personal research and teaching his higher level classes. Questions enthusiastically encouraged in lecture, once asked in person after class/during office hours are acknowledged halfheartedly and in a cold manner.

he is pretty boring and makes concepts like "hypothesis" seem really long-winded and acts as if no one knows what it is. i stopped attending classes after the midterm, came back during the last few weeks and realized i didn't miss anything. go to the conferences for a summary of his teachings and read the book, you'll get an A
Pretty bad. The lectures are unbearably boring - I stopped attending class after the first month but still ended up with a B thanks to a lot of studying. Avoid.

I had him as S/U (which I recommend), but he's not as bad as people put him. He is an AMAZING lecturer and extremely knowledgeable. I didn't go to many classes, and regretted it, not because the material was difficult, but because I found it very interesting and would've loved hearing his insight about it. 
Considering taking SOCI420 as extra!

Do not take this class!! The exams have very specific questions that are almost impossible to know unless you have memorized every slide. Slides are extremely detailed and lots of confusing wording. 36 slide presentation total with 10-30 slides in each. No preparation for the exams. Everything is posted on MyCourses so don't need to go to class.

Course content was too boring to not drool over my first lecture. Literally didnt attend after the second week, ever and still passed the final thanks to a general curve and memorizing the notes. Thought it would be a fun elective but ended up regretting it as it was anything but fun. Dont take this as ur CS group A elective @ engineering students!
Prof. Smith is genuinely a really smart person. Dude knows what he's talking about, especially in his niche area of expertise. Tough grader, but he curves it. Graded on only a Midterm and a Final.
If you want passing this course, you just need to remember everything in the slides. No need to come to the lecture, he will just read the slides. So you can 100% read it and remember it by yourself.

Only grades are exams and you have to memorize all the content from the semester. You don't have to do any of the readings and probably don't even need to go to class - but it's worth going because his lectures are great and he loves to engage with questions. Super interesting class but I wouldn't take him again because of the exam structure.

I went to class but you can manage to pass without going. You will need to remember all his PowerPoint for the exams: Midterm 35%; Final 65%. The questions are very specific so be prepared to learn by heart. Readings are not essential. His lectures are not very interactive and he speaks very fast which makes it hard to follow. Grades fairly.

I took soci211 with him, was an easy A. But SOCI235? Midterm was fair (got A-), but the final was way too hard. You need to memorize EVERY single slides. (Readings are not mandatory nor useful however!) Material is confusing. I do not recommend this class at all, unless you are good at learning by heart.

Prof Smith was very difficult and his lectures were very monotone and simply unenjoyable to attend. I would not recommend SOCI 235 to any of my friends as the course was very hard, there was only a midterm and final and both were very hard. Also, the course description and the actual course itself were very different!

Your final grade is determined by only a midterm (35%) and final (65%) and the grading criteria is quite unclear (we only received general feedback for the whole class). The zoom lectures were quite long and not very engaging (he just reads the slides) and there are participation marks with unclear criteria.

Smith is a nightmare. Had him for two semesters. His lectures are hard to follow as there are no visuals and he goes on a tangent, making you wonder what is relevant or not. He posts his notes online so you don't really need to go to class. Midterm was easy, final was unfair.

Really cool and smart guy. Obviously passionate and actually cares about teaching. Lectures are kind of all over the place though, so have to study what he posts. However, the midterm was very hard and was so rushed, didn't have time to answer a lot. He graded it up a lot though so I did fine and did well on the final

One midterm, one final. Midterm graded somewhat unfairly but if you knew /something/ for all the questions you got at least a B. Engaging lectures, but all the material is covered in the course pack and in the notes he posts later. Its hard to motivate yourself to go to class. Fun British accent.

He is actually a nice guy! Old in sociology, but got a lot of hair, which is rare. He curved up the grade A LOT. like 5-10 points. I was scared to receive a grade lower than A in mideterm but got so curved up. Thx Mike:)
Best class I've taken in my three years at McGill. He posts all his notes on MyCourses, read them once before our exams (only midterm and final) and got an A.

This is by far the most eye-opening course I've taken, the prof really showed us a big picture of what's happening from the past to the future in the technology-related work field. I would recommend to whoever's fond of encyclopedia, which is basically what this course is about: well-structured, mass information, key concepts from popular scholars

By far one of the BEST profs at McGill. Super engaging & interesting lectures, and he posts ALL his notes online. The class is only one midterm & final but they were both super fair and redirected exactly to the material he had provided us. 11/10 would take again.

He's a really engaging prof. He's actually really amazing, and he provides his lecture notes, which are actually the best. Fair warning though, the class has one midterm, and a final. While the assessments are difficult and detailed, they are very fair.
i love him! he has cold-humour that you usually miss bc youre so busy taking notes. he's accessible (if you reach out first) and i really like what he teaches!

Very clear lecturer, the material is well organized and explained. I found the readings to be a bit redundant to the lectures and barely took a look at them. His short-answer exams are extremely specific which can be hard if you don't memorize everything well. Overall a very interesting course!

At first, I didn't like him and then I changed my mind. He asks for  students participation). I didn't do my readings and still got an A. He gives detailed class-summary. He speaks really fast. Material is interesting (but I'm not passionate about it)  Not a must-take but its was a mandatory class (Industrial Relations) and I enjoyed it.

If you go to class and take notes, you can get an easy A. Everything on the exam is covered in class. All the readings are covered in his lectures and made much easier (don't even bother reading the coursepack). The only annoying part is the book assignment. I suggest splitting it into reading sections with a group.

Interesting course. All exam material is literally taken directly from his notes that he posts online & some from the readings. I went to only two classes in total so far, and got an A on the midterm. I just studied his lecture notes. Very nice prof, emails you back right away too. Wouldn't mind having him for another course.
I'm pretty sure he tries his very hardest to ensure that students don't do well. I had him for a 200-level course, but I was taking 300-levels that were easier :/

The class is actualy  interesting and in many ways eye opening. He also presents it very well and clearly. His powerpoints cover literaly everything and his exams are questions taken right out of his slides.If you study his slides you should do well on the exams. PLus he curves.
